action: Enforce MFA on all remote access, keep firewalls and VPN appliances patched and their management interfaces off the internet, hold offline immutable backups, and alert on Defender being disabled, logs cleared or WinSCP moving data out.
exec: A national agency profile of an active ransomware service; remote access without MFA and exposed management interfaces are its way in.
plain: India's cyber agency published a warning about The Gentlemen, a criminal group that rents out ransomware. It breaks in through remote-access equipment or stolen passwords, copies data, then locks Windows, Linux and virtual servers.

key_findings: The Gentlemen is a financially motivated ransomware-as-a-service group using double extortion; its Go-based payload is obfuscated with Garble and can self-propagate.
It targets Windows, Linux, BSD, NAS devices and VMware ESXi; reported sectors include healthcare, construction, finance and manufacturing.
Initial access is through internet-facing edge devices, RDP and VPN services, or compromised credentials.
Operators spread through Group Policy Objects and the NETLOGON share, disable Microsoft Defender, delete shadow copies and clear event and RDP logs.
Data is exfiltrated with WinSCP before encryption; the advisory lists file hashes, IP addresses and domains but no CVEs.
recommendations: Inventory internet-facing services, disable those not needed and keep management interfaces off the public internet.
Patch firewalls and VPN appliances and enforce MFA for all remote access.
Keep offline, encrypted, immutable backups isolated from production and test restoration.
Review Group Policy Objects, domain admin membership and changes to NETLOGON and SYSVOL regularly.
Do not pay ransoms; report incidents to CERT-In and law enforcement.

summary: India's CERT-In published advisory CIAD-2026-0060 on November 13 describing The Gentlemen, which it calls a financially motivated ransomware-as-a-service group that steals data before encrypting it. Its Go-based malware runs on Windows, Linux, BSD, NAS devices and VMware ESXi and can spread across a network unaided. Entry comes through internet-facing edge devices, RDP and VPN services or stolen credentials. Healthcare, construction, finance and manufacturing are named as victims.
title: CERT-In issues advisory CIAD-2026-0060 on The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service group

validation.note: Reviewed against the original CERT-In document.
